name: Ránu

anatomy.part: the kite's left corner, where the bridle is knotted
the tail-weight at the kite's foot, where the ribbon is tied on
the first fold of the ribbon as it lifts off the kite's tail
the second fold, where the ribbon snaps upward
the far tip of the ribbon
the far end of the string, rising up and left toward the Reel

myth: When Aun cut the string, he did not cut it clean. The Sun-Kite was still tied to his wrist, so it went up with the others, and its ribbon came loose and streamed behind it. Ennu had sewn that ribbon from the last of the sail-cloth, long enough to reach the far side of the sky. Mother Hesk saw it going and said nothing, because she was counting. At midsummer the Sun-Kite flies highest and the ribbon reaches furthest, and if you watch from the cliffs you can see it snap over the water like a wet rag on a line. Tavo tried to tear it. He failed, and laughed, which is how you will know him. The old ones say that if you tie a knot in your own hair and hold it to the wind, the Sun-Kite will see it and tug back. Mend your nets while you wait. The ribbon is still long, and the knot still holds.
verse:
Long ribbon, salt-stiff,
the Sun-Kite tows its tail out.
Hesk still counts the length.
